ENTERPRISE USER MANUAL

Complete Step-by-Step Operating Guide for Property Owners, Real Estate Developers & Engineering Teams
Scope of this Manual:
This guide explains how to operate the Planwise Enterprise web application from end to end: parcel intake, statutory feasibility checks, customer design briefs, mathematical CP-SAT layout generation, architectural floor plan blueprints, IS 1200 quantity takeoffs, turnkey cost estimation, and professional engineering review gates.
Product Version: 2.0.0-Enterprise
Document Reference: PW-DOC-MANUAL-2026
Publication Date: October 2026
Verification Standard: Zero-Fabrication Audit
Target Jurisdictions: Mumbai DCPR 2034 & BBMP 2026
Architecture: Canonical Building Model (CBM)

Statutory & Legal Warning Notice

MANDATORY STATUTORY NOTICE:
Planwise Enterprise is a computational land-to-home development platform that connects land constraints, statutory feasibility, architectural building design, quantity takeoffs, cost estimation, and controlled engineering handoff through a Canonical Building Model (CBM).

Planwise outputs support preliminary planning, feasibility analysis, and computational design synthesis. They do NOT constitute statutory municipal sanctions, structural engineering certifications, licensed architectural sign-offs, or authorization to commence construction.

All generated designs, structural elements, and quantity takeoffs must be reviewed, sealed, and submitted by a licensed Architect registered with the Council of Architecture (COA), a licensed Structural Engineer, and relevant municipal authorities (e.g., MCGM / BBMP) prior to physical execution.

Chapter 1: Introduction to Planwise Enterprise

Planwise Enterprise is an integrated computational land-to-home development platform. In conventional real estate workflows, land boundary surveys, zoning checks, floor planning, structural engineering, quantity surveying, and contractor budgeting exist in isolated silos. This causes months of delay, design discrepancies, and budget blowouts.

Planwise unifies these disciplines through a single Canonical Building Model (CBM). When a property owner or developer inputs land dimensions, the platform applies municipal development regulations, optimizes spatial layouts via mathematical constraint programming, extracts physical construction quantities adhering to national measurement standards, and computes turnkey budgets linked to localized rate catalogs.

1.1 Core System Capabilities

  • Zero Distortion Land Projection: Projects geodetic latitude and longitude coordinates into a local topocentric Site Engineering Coordinate System (SECS) with sub-millimeter precision.
  • Statutory Feasibility Automation: Evaluates directional setbacks, statutory road widening land surrenders, permissible Floor Space Index (FSI), ground coverage, and height limits.
  • Constraint Programming Floor Plan Synthesis: Uses Google OR-Tools CP-SAT to synthesize room layouts that guarantee zero room overlap, compliance with National Building Code (NBC 2016) room sizes, and forbidden adjacency rules.
  • Rigorous 3D Solid Geometry: Evaluates watertight 2-manifold CAD solids via Manifold3D, guaranteeing positive volume and topological integrity.
  • IS 1200 Quantity Extraction: Deducts door, window, and shaft voids from wall masonry and concrete slabs using standardized thresholds.
  • Controlled Engineering Handoff: Enforces seven sequential review gates (G0 to G6) and packages release baselines into open buildingSMART IFC4 models.

1.2 Intended User Personas

User Persona Primary Workflow Key Deliverables Used
Property Owner / Homebuilder Tests what house typologies fit their land, reviews setbacks, and explores budget options. Customer Floor Plan View, Feasibility Summary, Turnkey Cost Waterfall.
Real Estate Developer Rapid plot yield analysis, comparison of single-family vs duplex options across plot portfolios. FSI Yield Metrics, Pareto Option Cards, Financial Waterfall Breakdown.
Design Manager / Architect Synthesizes compliant room configurations, inspects dimension ticks, and mutates room widths. Architectural CAD Blueprint Viewer, SVG Vector Drawing Export, CBM JSON.
Civil Engineer / Quantity Surveyor Audits itemized trade quantities, inspects opening deductions, and signs off review gates. IS 1200 BOQ Spreadsheet, Engineer Review Dashboard, IFC4 Model.

Chapter 3: Creating a Land Project (Step 1: LAND)

Every development begins with defining the site parcel in Step 1: LAND.

Figure 3.1: Land Intake Screen (Customer Mode) showing project location, declared area of 1,500 sq ft, and road parameters.

3.1 Entering Land Details (Customer Mode)

  1. Project Location & Address: Enter the site address (e.g., Bandra West, Mumbai).
  2. Jurisdiction: Select the municipal building code. Planwise includes verified rule packs for MUMBAI_DCPR_2034 and BBMP_BENGALURU_2026.
  3. Declared Plot Area: Enter the legal registered area from your title deed (e.g., 1500) and select the unit (sq ft or sq m).
  4. Plot Geometry Shape:
    • Regular (Rectangular / Square): The engine computes an optimal 16:9 aspect ratio envelope.
    • Irregular: Prompts for coordinate vertices or map drawing.
  5. Existing Road Width: Enter the current physical road width (e.g., 16 ft / 4.88 m).
  6. Proposed Master Plan Road Width: Enter the statutory widened road width (e.g., 40 ft / 12.19 m).
  7. Road-Facing Orientation: Select which parcel edge faces the access road (North, South, East, or West).

Click Confirm Land & Run Feasibility to save parcel parameters and advance to Step 2.

3.2 Technical Mode: Mapbox Canvas & Boundary Manipulation

Switching to TECHNICAL mode displays the full GIS map canvas:

  • Adding Vertices: Click anywhere on the map to add parcel boundary nodes. A minimum of 3 vertices is required to form a closed polygon.
  • Editing Vertices: Click and drag any vertex to adjust boundaries.
  • Debounced Auto-Save: The map automatically debounces updates and saves changes to PUT /api/v1/projects/{id}/geometries within 600ms.

3.3 Critical Area Concepts

Area Metric Definition & Calculation Significance for Homeowners
Declared Plot Area Gross registered land area (e.g. 1,500 sq ft = 139.35 m²). Your legal ownership boundary recorded on sale deeds.
Road Widening Surrender Land surrendered along road frontage: depth = max(0, (ProposedRoad - ExistingRoad)/2). Must be left unbuilt and surrendered to the municipality.
Net Developable Area Net Area = Declared Area - Surrender Area. The statutory base area used to compute your permissible FSI.
Buildable Footprint Buildable Area = Net Area - Directional Setbacks. The physical ground area inside which your house walls can sit.

Chapter 4: Site Evidence & Statutory Feasibility (Step 2: FEASIBILITY)

Once land parameters are saved, Planwise evaluates statutory feasibility in Step 2: FEASIBILITY.

Figure 4.1: Feasibility Summary Screen showing statutory compliance status, setback deductions, and permissible BUA.

4.1 Reviewing Feasibility Metrics

  • Statutory Feasibility Status: Displays FEASIBLE (green badge) if the parcel accommodates residential construction. If setbacks leave less than 10 m² buildable area, the system alerts INFEASIBLE_SETBACK_COLLAPSE.
  • Road Widening Surrender: Displays the calculated surrender depth and deducted area.
  • Directional Building Setbacks:
    • Front Setback: Required distance from the road boundary (e.g., 4.5m for Mumbai roads 9m-12m).
    • Rear Setback: Rear property clearance (statutory 3.0m).
    • Side Setbacks: Lateral side buffers (statutory 1.5m each).
  • Permissible Built-Up Area (BUA): The maximum allowable constructed floor area across all storeys: Permissible BUA = Net Area * (Base FSI + Premium FSI + TDR FSI)
  • Usable Carpet Area: Estimated usable floor area calculated at 70% of permissible BUA per RERA rules.
  • Maximum Permissible Height: Statutory height cap corresponding to road width (e.g., 16.0m for roads under 9m, up to 120.0m for roads 27m or wider).

4.2 Site Evidence & Confidence Tiers (L0 to L3)

The Site Evidence & Truth Panel in the top-right corner shows your site's confidence rating:

Tier Confidence Category Data Provenance Release Status
L0 Unverified Declaration User manually entered area without spatial boundary nodes. BLOCKED (Draft only)
L1 Desktop Geometry Drawn on map satellite canvas (±2.5m error). BLOCKED (Layout exploration only)
L2 Municipal Cadastral Official municipality GIS parcel boundary shapefile. CONDITIONAL (Sanction review)
L3 Licensed Land Survey Total Station / RTK-GNSS licensed land surveyor boundary with monuments. UNLOCKED (Construction Release)

Chapter 5: Entering the Customer Design Brief (Step 3: DESIGN — Intake)

In Step 3: DESIGN, you specify your family's living requirements.

Figure 5.1: Customer Design Intake Screen for selecting bedrooms, bathrooms, floor levels, and architectural styles.

5.1 Configuring Requirements

  1. Bedrooms (BHK Typology): Select 1 BHK, 2 BHK, 3 BHK, 4 BHK, or 5+ BHK.
  2. Bathrooms: Select 1 Bath, 2 Baths, 3 Baths, or 4+ Baths.
  3. Floor Configuration:
    • 1 Floor (Single Level): All living spaces arranged on the ground level (L0).
    • 2 Floors (G+1 Duplex): Living, kitchen, and guest suite on ground level (L0); master suite, secondary bedrooms, and family lounge on first floor (L1), connected by an internal RCC staircase.
  4. Architectural Style:
    • Contemporary: Open-plan living/dining, expansive window glazing.
    • Minimalist: Compact circulation corridors, efficient modular room proportions.
    • Traditional: Distinct kitchen compartmentalization, formal entrance foyer.
    • Modern Indian: Dedicated prayer/pooja alcove, separate utility wash yard.
  5. Parking Spaces: Configure covered or stilt parking allocation (1 to 2 ECS).

Click Synthesize Architectural Options (CP-SAT) to trigger the layout solver.

Chapter 6: Generating & Comparing Design Options (Step 3: DESIGN — Options)

Planwise uses Google OR-Tools CP-SAT to synthesize floor plans mathematically.

Figure 6.1: Generated Design Options View showing Pareto candidate cards, area metrics, and estimated budgets.

6.1 Mathematical Principles of Generation

  • 100mm Integer Grid: Rooms are placed on a 100mm (0.1m) coordinate grid.
  • Zero Overlap: Model interval variables and AddNoOverlap2D guarantee that rooms never collide.
  • NBC 2016 Room Area Bounds: Every room satisfies minimum areas (Living ≥ 9.5m², Master Bed ≥ 9.5m², Kitchen ≥ 4.5m², Bath ≥ 1.8m²).
  • Perimeter Daylighting: Habitable rooms earn objective bonuses when positioned along exterior envelope walls.
  • Wet Area Clustering: Wet spaces (baths, kitchen, utility) are clustered to minimize plumbing runs.
  • Pareto Frontier Filtering: Filters candidates down to optimal options balancing spatial efficiency, daylight, and circulation.

6.2 Comparing Design Cards

Each synthesized candidate card presents key metrics:

  • Gross Built-Up Area (BUA): Total constructed area (e.g., 139.35 m² / 1,500 sq ft).
  • Usable Carpet Area: Net usable interior floor area (e.g., 105.8 m² / 1,139 sq ft).
  • Spatial Efficiency: Ratio of usable carpet area to BUA (typically 75% - 82%).
  • Estimated Budget: Real-time estimate from the preliminary BOQ (e.g., ₹39.2 Lakhs).
  • 2D Plan Thumbnail: Interactive preview showing room layout and circulation.

Click on any candidate card to select it, or click Choose This Design & Review Cost to proceed.

Chapter 7: Reading Architectural Floor Plans (Step 3: DESIGN — Viewer)

Selecting an option displays the architectural CAD blueprint.

Figure 7.1: Architectural Floor Plan Blueprint showing room layouts, door swing arcs, sliding windows, and dimension strings.

7.1 Architectural Drafting Conventions

  1. Walls:
    • External Walls: Thick 1.6pt black strokes with subtle grey fill (230mm / 9" load-bearing structural walls).
    • Internal Partitions: Thin 1.0pt strokes (115mm / 4.5" non-load-bearing AAC blocks).
  2. Doors & Swing Arcs: Rendered with a solid door leaf at 90° and a dashed quarter-circle arc showing swing clearance.
  3. Windows: Rendered as double lines along exterior walls with outer cut lines and inner glass centerlines.
  4. Stairs (for Duplexes): Rendered with parallel step tread lines, landing dividers, and an arrow pointing upward with the label "UP".
  5. Dimension Strings: Lines with 45° architectural tick marks showing imperial feet-and-inches (e.g., 14'-6") and metric millimeters.
  6. Room Labels: Bold room titles with net carpet area (e.g., MASTER BEDROOM, 14.2 m²).

7.2 Interactive Room Dimension Mutation

Clicking on any room in the floor plan opens the Room Inspector Panel:

Figure 7.2: Interactive Room Mutation showing dimension adjustments and live area re-validation.
  • Width & Depth Controls: Use +0.2m / -0.2m buttons to fine-tune room dimensions.
  • NBC Re-validation: Checks whether modified dimensions continue to satisfy NBC minimums.
  • Instant Cost Recalculation: Modifying boundaries instantly recalculates wall lengths, finishes, and the cost estimate.

Chapter 8: Quantity Takeoff, BOQ & Cost Estimation (Step 4: COST)

In Step 4: COST, Planwise translates building geometry into an itemized construction budget.

Figure 8.1: Cost Summary Screen displaying turnkey construction estimate, cost per sq ft BUA, quality tiers, and financial waterfall.

8.1 IS 1200 Measurement Standards

Quantities are calculated from model solids adhering to IS 1200: Indian Standard Method of Measurement:

  • IS 1200 Part 3 (Masonry): Gross wall volume (Length * Height * Thickness) less door and window openings greater than 0.1 m².
  • IS 1200 Part 2 (Concrete): Column volumes (Width * Depth * Height) and slab volumes, deducting stair openings greater than 0.1 m².
  • IS 1200 Part 12 (Plastering): Wall faces and ceiling soffits, deducting openings greater than 0.5 m² per Clause 4.2.
  • IS 1200 Part 11 (Flooring): Room carpet areas for tiling, and perimeters less doorway widths for skirting.

8.2 The Turnkey Cost Waterfall

[ Direct Gross Hard Cost (Sum of BOQ Lines) ]
                      |
                      +---> + 8.0% Contractor Prelims & Site Overheads
                      |
                      +---> + 5.0% Physical Contingency Buffer
                      |
           [ Construction Subtotal ]
                      |
                      +---> + 18.0% Statutory Goods & Services Tax (GST)
                      |
        [ TOTAL TURNKEY ESTIMATED CONSTRUCTION COST ]

Example: 1,500 sq ft Residence (Standard Tier):

  • Direct Hard Construction Cost: ₹31,45,200.00
  • Contractor Prelims & Site Overheads (8%): ₹2,51,616.00
  • Physical Contingency Buffer (5%): ₹1,57,260.00
  • Construction Subtotal: ₹35,54,076.00
  • Statutory GST (18% on Subtotal): ₹6,39,733.68
  • Total Estimated Turnkey Cost: ₹41,93,809.68
  • Cost per Sq Ft BUA: ₹2,795.87 / sq ft

8.3 Quality Tier Switching

  • ECONOMY: Country brick, vitrified tiles (600x600mm), standard flush doors (~₹2,350 / sq ft BUA).
  • STANDARD (Default): AAC blocks, nano-polished tiles (800x800mm), UPVC windows (~₹2,795 / sq ft BUA).
  • PREMIUM: Italian composite marble, teakwood main door frame, double-glazed windows (~₹3,450 / sq ft BUA).
  • LUXURY: Imported marble, concealed VRV air conditioning, automated smart home electricals (~₹4,200 / sq ft BUA).

Click Proceed to Step 5: BUILD to prepare for project release.

Chapter 9: Build Review, Release Locking & Handoff Packages (Step 5: BUILD)

In Step 5: BUILD, you review and freeze the approved design baseline.

Figure 9.1: Build Review Screen displaying customer statutory acknowledgements, release gating summary, and build confirmation controls.

9.1 Customer Statutory Acknowledgements

Before locking the build release, the user must acknowledge three statutory statements:

  1. [x] I understand that soil bearing capacity and foundation design require a site-specific geotechnical borehole test.
  2. [x] I acknowledge that architectural drawings must be sanctioned by the local municipal corporation prior to construction.
  3. [x] I confirm that the selected quality tier and preliminary budget reflect my requested specifications.

Click Lock Build Release (G6 Release Gate) to freeze the design baseline.

9.2 The Release Handoff Package

Locking the build triggers a deterministic cryptographic freeze:

  • Release ID: Assigns an immutable release identifier (e.g., rel-pilot-20261002-aedf9830).
  • Cryptographic SHA-256 Fingerprint: Generates a 64-character hash over the model geometry, rates, and quantities. Any subsequent edit generates a new design version, preventing silent tampering.
  • Handoff Package Contents:
    • model_cbm.json — Canonical Building Model definition.
    • model_ifc4.ifc — buildingSMART IFC4 architectural model with georeferenced metadata.
    • floor_plan_ground.svg — Vector CAD floor plan drawing.
    • bill_of_quantities.csv & .json — Itemized IS 1200 trade quantities and rates.
    • cost_waterfall_summary.pdf — Turnkey financial breakdown.
    • validation_report.json — Manifold3D watertightness and compliance logs.

10.2 Recording Decisions & Digital Stamp Signing

  • Review Issues: Inspect warnings and compliance issues (e.g., WAR-GEO-001: Geotechnical investigation required).
  • Override Permissions: Senior review engineers can record justification notes to override non-critical warnings.
  • Digital Stamp Signing: Entering a licensed registration number (e.g., PE-STR-MUM-48291) applies a cryptographic signature seal to all exported drawing sheets and reports.

10.3 Downloading Project Documents

  • Download A3 Drawing Sheets (PDF): Opens the DrawingSheetsModal to download architectural drawings (Title Sheet, Site Plan, Ground Plan, Terrace Plan, Sections, Schedules).
  • Download Customer Home Report (PDF): Downloads the customer project summary report.
  • Export IFC4 Model: Downloads the open BIM model for Revit, ArchiCAD, or Solibri.

Chapter 11: Practical Troubleshooting Guide

Diagnostic reference for common issues encountered during project execution:

Issue / Symptom Likely Cause Recommended Safe Action When to Escalate
"Infeasible Setback Collapse" on Feasibility Plot area is too small or setbacks exceed plot width (less than 10 m² buildable area). Verify road widths. If road width was entered too high, reduce to measured access road. If plot is genuinely narrow, escalate to an architect for setback variances.
"Road Widening Strip Consumes Entire Plot" Proposed road width was entered incorrectly (e.g., 30m instead of 12m). Check city master plan road width. Update road width in Step 1. If widening line is contested, verify with municipal development plan remarks.
CP-SAT Layout Generation Times Out (> 10s) Brief requested too many rooms for the buildable footprint (e.g., 5 BHK in 600 sq ft). Reduce bedroom count, or change floor configuration to 2 Floors (G+1 Duplex). If solver fails repeatedly on valid plots, check backend API gateway logs.
"Cannot Lock Build: Release Gated by Site Evidence" Project is at site confidence level L0 or L1. System blocks releases without survey data. Upload a Total Station survey or municipal CTS cadastral vector in Site Evidence Panel. Escalate to licensed land surveyor to conduct on-site monument survey.
Doorway Opens Across Room Boundary Room dimensions were manually mutated beyond host wall extent. Click Reset Layout in Floor Plan Viewer to restore optimal placement. If reset fails, re-generate options from Step 3.
Cost Estimate Displays "₹0.00" Rate snapshot not loaded or model lacks compiled CBM elements. Click Retry on Cost Summary card. Verify network connection to API gateway. If rates remain empty, restart local backend service (apps/api-gateway).
3D Solid View Shows Missing Walls Browser WebGL context lost or Manifold3D library compiling. Refresh page or toggle 3D Solid button in CAD toolbar. Ensure Chrome hardware acceleration is enabled in browser settings.
IFC Export Fails or File is 0 Bytes Disk permissions error in local artifacts/ folder. Verify local disk write permissions in workspace directory. Escalate to system administrator.
Changes to Declared Area Do Not Reflect in Design Cached browser session holding previous design version. Click My Project -> Clear & Start Fresh, then re-enter declared plot area. Ensure API gateway is running and not returning 304 Not Modified.
Browser Shows "API Connection Failed / Offline" Backend FastAPI server on port 5001 is stopped. Run uvicorn apps.api_gateway.main:app --port 5001 in terminal workspace. Verify port 5001 is not blocked by a local firewall.

Chapter 12: System Limitations & Safe Use Boundaries

To ensure safe, ethical, and legally compliant use, Planwise Enterprise discloses the following operational boundaries:

12.1 Security & Multi-Tenancy Prototype Status

  • PostgreSQL Row-Level Security (RLS): Not active in the current prototype. The application runs as a local single-tenant workspace. Do not deploy to an untrusted public network without adding authentication middleware.
  • Session Isolation: Projects are stored in an in-memory application cache. Clearing the server restarts the baseline project state.

12.2 Architectural & Engineering Scope Limits

  • Multi-Floor Generation: The CP-SAT solver optimizes ground floor layouts directly; upper levels on multi-storey duplexes are generated sequentially using staircase core alignment.
  • Structural Finite Element Analysis (FEA): The platform places structural RCC columns along standard room intersections. It does not perform 3D structural frame analysis, wind load calculations, or seismic moment distribution. A licensed Structural Engineer must size all reinforcement rebar and footing dimensions.
  • Dynamic MEP Routing: The system calculates fixture point counts and vertical plumbing stacks; it does not model 3D spatial piping slope or electrical conduit runs.
  • Municipal Sanctions: Planwise generates compliance dossiers, but does not connect automatically to municipal sanction portals (e.g., MCGM AutoDCR or BBMP Suvarna). Formal submission requires an architect's council registration number.
  • Geotechnical Foundations: Default foundation excavation depths assume standard empirical soil conditions (150 kN/m²). Actual footing design requires physical soil borehole testing.

12.3 Safe Use Notice

OPERATIONAL USE POLICY:
Planwise outputs support preliminary planning, feasibility analysis, and computational design synthesis. They do NOT constitute statutory municipal sanctions, structural engineering certifications, licensed architectural sign-offs, or authorization to commence construction.

Always obtain formal reviews and statutory approvals from qualified professionals and relevant municipal authorities before breaking ground on any construction site.
